meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty-five minutes, and I'd like to know who decided Owen gets a zero, and whether anyone spoke to him before they did.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Owen found out on his phone, in the middle of a class. So what do you have, Hale?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
I'm writing that down. "Like, being stuck" is a seventeen-year-old answering a question he didn't know was coming, and the note is yours, not mine. Show me the page.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

I'm writing down October 15. Students change their argument between an outline and a draft, Hale, and I'd like to know what makes that proof of anything. Put the outline and the essay in front of me, and the page with your note on it, and I'll read them myself.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

I'm writing down Thursday at 8:15, and your email by Friday at 3 PM. A rewrite is where this ends, Hale, not where it starts, so the zero comes out of the gradebook today, and I still haven't seen one page of what you've described. Is that room empty when he sits it, or is his class there?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook, the outline, the essay and your note from November 2 put in front of me, and written confirmation that nothing goes on Owen's record. I expect your written offer by Friday at 3 PM.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position; she wrote down the rewrite offer but did not accept it, and she still wants the zero out of the gradebook today, the documents in front of her, and an answer on whether the rewrite is private.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one plain sentence and moved on, which gave her a flat okay, because that was the procedural failure she came in angry about.
What cost ground: You described the conversation and the outline without showing her any page, so she could not check them, and you offered the rewrite before she had seen a single document.
Try next time: When you raised the outline from October 15, put it on the desk next to the essay right then, before you said anything about a rewrite.
